scenes.title: Marrakech
scenes.subtitle: Jemaa el-Fna square and the Koutoubia

scenes.caption: Photo 1923
scenes.text: Meanings could thus be "The Assembly of Death/the Dead", referring to public executions on the plaza around 1050 CE; "The Mosque at the End of the World"; or a reference to a mosque with a distinctive courtyard or square in front…

scenes.caption: Photo 1923
scenes.text: Marrakesh was founded by the Almoravid dynasty in 1070 by Abu Bakr ibn Umar and subsequently developed by his successors.

scenes.caption: Photo 1925
scenes.text: After a destructive struggle, Marrakech fell to the Almohads in 1147, who undertook many construction projects throughout the city.

scenes.caption: Photo 1925
scenes.text: Notably, a new royal kasbah (citadel) was erected further south by Ya'qub al-Mansur after 1184.

scenes.caption: Photo 1925
scenes.text: On January 24, 1864, a massive explosion took place in the area of the square, reportedly caused by the criminal negligence of certain officials trying to avoid a government inspection.

scenes.caption: Photo 1925
scenes.text: In 1922 the government (under French administration at the time), passed the first laws aimed at protecting and preserving the square's cultural space and heritage.

scenes.caption: Photo 1925
scenes.text: In 2001 the square was proclaimed an Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO, and in 2008 it was included in UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

scenes.caption: Photo 1929
scenes.text: An earthquake with a 6.8 magnitude that struck Morocco in the evening of Friday the 8th of September 2023 highly damaged the Kharbouch Mosque and collapsed its minaret, which overlooked the square.

scenes.caption: Photo 1919
scenes.text: Beginning in May 2025, the square underwent a major renovation program scheduled for completion by the end of the year.

scenes.title: The place
scenes.text: Heart of the medina founded by the Almoravids in the 11th century, overlooked by the Almohad minaret of the Koutoubia (12th century). Its storytellers, musicians and traders made it an oral heritage recognised by UNESCO…
